ca-chp-cmsp.title: CHP California Motorcyclist Safety Program
ca-chp-cmsp.note: The program owner's own page, and the authority for courseType CA. CHP is statutorily responsible under Vehicle Code sections 2930-2935 and administers the CMSP through a primary contractor, currently Total Control Training Inc — so the curriculum is California's own, not MSF's and not a federal standard. Gives the 15-hour structure and the Premier Program. Publishes no course price.

ca-cmsp-new-riders.title: CMSP New Rider Course Guide
ca-cmsp-new-riders.note: The CMSP programme's current public site, run by the CHP's contractor rather than on a state domain — the route DMV ultimately sends riders to, and a better findCourse citation than the DMV page because this is where a rider actually searches locations and books. Publishes no price itself: classCost surveys rates its listed providers publish, and those are uniform statewide rather than provider-set, quoted identically by MRE Corp and Central Coast Motorcycle Training as $425 at 21 and over and $395 at 20 and under. Supersedes ca-msp.org, which DMV still links and which no longer resolves.

ca-dmv-driver-licenses.title: CA DMV Driver's License Guide
ca-dmv-driver-licenses.note: Carries the DMV class table that lists Motorcycle (Class M1 or M2) as a driver's licence class, which is what links the general five-year term to motorcycles. Also sets out the out-of-state applicant path: a holder of another state's licence must still pass the knowledge test(s), with no reciprocity waiver offered anywhere on it.

ca-dmv-handbook-getting-license.title: CA Driver Handbook: Getting a Permit and License
ca-dmv-handbook-getting-license.note: Section 2 of the Driver Handbook, and the source for minAge 16 — it requires an applicant under 18 to be at least 16 years old. That is the general driver's licence floor rather than a motorcycle-specific rule; it reaches M1 and M2 because they are driver's licence classes. California's motorcycle-specific age rule is the separate under-21 requirement to hold a permit six months, which is recorded in meta.note.

ca-dmv-instruction-permits.title: CA DMV Instruction and Learner's Permit Guide
ca-dmv-instruction-permits.note: The only DMV page found that publishes a motorcycle passing score. It runs the car and motorcycle permits as separate sections, and the motorcycle one states its questions come from the California Motorcycle Handbook and a passing score is 80% — so the figure is motorcycle-specific, not the car test's. The same motorcycle knowledge test serves the permit and the licence. Gives no question count and no time limit; its only timing statement is that tests stop at 4:30 p.m., a closing cutoff rather than a per-exam clock. Do not confuse this 80% with the CMSP course's own 80% written-evaluation threshold, which is a different exam.

ca-dmv-licensing-fees.title: CA DMV Licensing Fee Schedule
ca-dmv-licensing-fees.note: dmvCost is a single $46 rather than a range: the same fee covers an original or renewed Class M1/M2 and adding M1/M2 to a Class C. The $59 figure on this page is the commercial-licence equivalent and is out of scope. Carries no licence term.

ca-dmv-motorcycle-handbook.title: CA DMV Motorcycle Handbook
ca-dmv-motorcycle-handbook.note: Form DL 665, free from DMV, 7MB PDF saved to primary-sources. The authority for transferOutOfStateEndorsement none: DMV will not waive the motorcycle skills test on an out-of-state training programme or any in-state or out-of-state course completion card, and the only waiver is a DL 389 from the CMSP course. Read with the DMV's out-of-state applicant path, which requires passing the knowledge tests, nothing a rider holds elsewhere removes a California test. States that knowledge test questions are drawn from this handbook and the California Driver Handbook, but gives no question count, no passing score and no time limit — which is why CA's exam fields stay null.

ca-dmv-motorcycle-licenses.title: CA DMV Motorcycle License Guide
ca-dmv-motorcycle-licenses.note: The main DMV page for M1 and M2, and the authority for requirementType all: it states a motorcycle license covers a motorized bicycle, moped or bicycle with an attached motor, so unlike FL, GA and TX there is no engine-size exemption. Also carries the under-21 and over-21 paths, the six-month permit rule and the DL 389 skills-test waiver. minLicense reads None from the over-21 path, which asks for a California DL only 'if you have one'. States no minimum age and no knowledge-test detail.

ca-dmv-motorcyclists-guide.title: CA DMV Motorcyclists Guide
ca-dmv-motorcyclists-guide.note: Rider-facing hub linking licensing, registration, the Motorcycle Handbook and sample tests. Corroborates the CMSP structure and the DL 389 waiver without being the primary source for either. Carries a stale link: it tells riders to visit ca-msp.org to sign up, and that domain now times out and redirects to a Motorcycle Safety Foundation marketing page. Do not treat ca-msp.org as the CMSP booking route.

ca-veh-12816.title: CA Statute on Driver License Expiration
ca-veh-12816.note: Vehicle Code 12816(a): every original driver's license expires on the applicant's fifth birthday following the application. It says driver's license, not motorcycle license, because in California M1 and M2 are classes of driver's license rather than a separate credential — DMV's own class table on ca-dmv-driver-licenses lists Motorcycle (Class M1 or M2) alongside the car classes. expirationType 5year rests on those two together.

fl-hsmv-course-locations.title: FLHSMV Motorcycle Course Directory
fl-hsmv-course-locations.publisher: Florida Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles
fl-hsmv-course-locations.note: FRTP Sponsors by county; page carries no prices. classCost surveys listed Sponsors' published rates. Some counties list no Sponsors.

fl-hsmv-endorsement-faqs.title: FLHSMV Motorcycle Endorsement FAQ
fl-hsmv-endorsement-faqs.publisher: Florida Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles

fl-hsmv-endorsement-info.title: FLHSMV Motorcycle Endorsement Guide
fl-hsmv-endorsement-info.publisher: Florida Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles

fl-hsmv-fees.title: FLHSMV Fee Schedule
fl-hsmv-fees.publisher: Florida Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles
fl-hsmv-fees.note: Statewide fee schedule. dmvCost = $25.00 replacement license + $7.00 endorsement, plus a $6.25 service fee that applies only at a tax collector office — hence the range rather than one figure.

fl-hsmv-frtp-courses.title: FLHSMV Rider Training Course Guide
fl-hsmv-frtp-courses.publisher: Florida Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles
fl-hsmv-frtp-courses.note: Distinguishes BRC/BRCu from 3WBRC and S/TEP. Course required for all riders regardless of age since July 1, 2008.

fl-stat-322-0255.title: FL Statute on the Motorcycle Safety Education Program
fl-stat-322-0255.note: Statutory basis for the FRTP: requires a minimum 12 hours of instruction with at least 6 on a motorcycle, and authorizes FLHSMV to adopt Motorcycle Safety Foundation curricula — statutory corroboration for courseType. Caps a Sponsor's registration fee at $20, refundable on completion. States no passing score and no time limit. Year in the URL increments annually — recheck each pass.

fl-stat-322-21.title: FL Statute on Driver License Fees
fl-stat-322-21.note: Statutory authority behind the FLHSMV fee schedule. Year in the URL increments annually — recheck each pass.

ga-dds-brc.title: GA DDS Basic Riders Course Guide
ga-dds-brc.note: GMSP course page. Publishes tuition, graduation requirements, and the 90-day test waiver. Never names the Motorcycle Safety Foundation as the curriculum owner, so courseType MSFBRC is inferred from two things it does state: the 5-hour classroom plus 10-hour range structure MSF publishes for the BRC, and that graduates hold an MSF Course Completion Card. Page is marked noindex.

ga-dds-class-m.title: GA DDS Class M License Checklist
ga-dds-class-m.note: Step-by-step Class M page. Age requirement is the first bullet. Lists no prior-license prerequisite.

ga-dds-drivers-manual-testing.title: GA DDS Driver's Manual: Testing Section
ga-dds-drivers-manual-testing.note: Section 3 of the 2023-2024 Driver's Manual, and the most procedurally complete account DDS publishes of a knowledge exam session: walk-in only, the full list of rules in force during the test, and 15 of 20 to pass on each of Road Signs and Road Rules. States no time limit — checked, and deliberately left unresolved rather than recorded as none. Distinct from ga-dds-motorcycle-manual, which is the Motorcycle Operator's Manual.

ga-dds-fees-terms.title: GA DDS Fee and Term Schedule
ga-dds-fees-terms.note: Single table carrying both the Class M license fee/term and the MP permit fee/term. dmvCost = $32 Class M license, rising to $42 for riders taking the DDS skills-test route, which requires the $10 Class MP permit; the course route needs no permit. $5 discount for eligible online transactions is not reflected in listed fees.

ga-dds-gmsp-registration.title: GA DDS Motorcycle Course Registration Portal
ga-dds-gmsp-registration.note: State-run booking portal for all GMSP courses and locations — the single funnel DDS directs riders to.

ga-dds-mopeds.title: GA DDS Moped and Scooter Rules

ga-dds-motorcycle-hub.title: GA DDS Motorcycle License Guide
ga-dds-motorcycle-hub.note: Top-level motorcycle explainer. Defines motorcycle as excluding mopeds 50cc or less and groups all 51cc+ machines in one category. Lays out both paths to Class M.

ga-dds-motorcycle-manual.title: GA DDS Motorcycle Operator's Manual
ga-dds-motorcycle-manual.note: Free state-published manual and the stated source material for the Knowledge Exam and Rider Skills Test. Direct PDF is 19MB; DDS also links two different third-party flipbook mirrors on different pages.

ga-dds-motorcycle-permit.title: GA DDS Class MP Permit Checklist
ga-dds-motorcycle-permit.note: MP permit path: age 16, $10, 6-month term, one renewal only. Carries the permit restrictions (daylight only, no passengers, no limited-access roads).

ga-dds-road-test.title: GA DDS Road Test Appointment Guide
ga-dds-road-test.note: Motorcycle skills test scheduling. Reservations require a valid MP permit; rider must furnish and insure their own motorcycle and pass a safety inspection.

ga-dds-test-exams.title: GA DDS Testing and Exams Guide
ga-dds-test-exams.note: Knowledge Exam is a Road Rules test plus a Road Signs test, 15 of 20 required on each. Also covers the Rider Skills Test and the one-year expiry on motorcycle knowledge scores.

ga-dds-transfer.title: GA DDS Out-of-State License Transfer Guide
ga-dds-transfer.note: Covers non-commercial classes from all 49 other states, DC and US Territories. Knowledge and road tests are triggered only if the out-of-state license has been expired more than two years. Does not name Class M explicitly. URL is the page's own canonical; dds.georgia.gov/out-state-transfer is a short alias that also resolves here.

tx-dps-fees.title: TX DPS Fee Schedule
tx-dps-fees.note: dmvCost spans the two motorcycle paths listed here: $16 to add motorcycle to an existing Texas license, $33 for a Class M-only license. The $48 'new license and motorcycle' line bundles the car license and is deliberately outside the range. Also the authority for expirationType — eight years at 18-84, two years at 85+.

tx-dps-license-classes.title: TX DPS Guide to License Classes
tx-dps-license-classes.note: Defines Class M as authorizing an individual to drive a motorcycle, and records that other classes do not cover motorcycles. States no engine-size floor.

tx-dps-motorcycle-license.title: TX DPS Motorcycle License Guide
tx-dps-motorcycle-license.note: The single DPS page covering the Class M path: course requirement, minor requirements, skills test and its waivers, and the J and I restrictions. minLicense reads None from it — an unrestricted Texas A, B or C license waives the skills test rather than gating the credential. Does not state the engine-size boundary that requirementType needs.

tx-stat-521-001.title: TX Statute on Driver License Classes
tx-stat-521-001.note: Transportation Code chapter 521, the driver licensing chapter. Sec. 521.084 is the operative link for requirementType: a Class M license authorizes operating a motorcycle as defined by Sec. 541.201, which is where the moped carve-out lives. The chapter itself never mentions mopeds.

tx-stat-541-201.title: TX Statute on Vehicle Definitions
tx-stat-541-201.note: Transportation Code chapter 541. Sec. 541.201(9) defines a motorcycle as excluding a moped, and 541.201(8) defines a moped compoundly: 50cc or less, no more than 30 mph, under five brake horsepower, and no gear shifting. requirementType 50ccUp records the headline; unlike FL and GA the Texas test is not displacement alone, so a geared or fast 49cc machine needs Class M.

tx-tdlr-curriculum.title: TDLR Motorcycle Course Curriculum Rules
tx-tdlr-curriculum.publisher: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
tx-tdlr-curriculum.note: The authority for courseType. Texas mandates a standard, not a curriculum: an entry-level course must meet the 2011 Model National Standards for Entry-Level Motorcycle Rider Training issued by USDOT/NHTSA, and TDLR approves each school's own materials against it. MSF BRC is one approved option, never a requirement — which is why courseType is MNS2011 and not MSFBRC. Also the reason the exam fields are null: the rule requires a curriculum to include a knowledge examination but specifies no item count, passing score or time limit, delegating all of it to the approved curriculum.

tx-tdlr-find-schools.title: TDLR Motorcycle School Directory
tx-tdlr-find-schools.publisher: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
tx-tdlr-find-schools.note: State-published map and CSV of licensed independent schools, which riders contact directly — the basis for findCourse stateLocator. Carries no prices and no course rosters; TDLR directs riders to each school for both. TDLR publishes no tuition, so classCost surveys rates the listed schools publish themselves: $225-$275 Houston, $290 Waco, $345 Mount Pleasant. Some schools quote only inside a booking flow.

tx-tdlr-motorcycle-hub.title: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Safety Program
tx-tdlr-motorcycle-hub.publisher: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
tx-tdlr-motorcycle-hub.note: Program home for the agency that licenses Texas motorcycle schools and instructors and approves their curricula. DPS issues the license; TDLR regulates the training.

tx-tdlr-motorcycle-manual.title: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual
tx-tdlr-motorcycle-manual.publisher: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
tx-tdlr-motorcycle-manual.note: Texas rider manual, 2020-2021 edition, 8.2MB PDF saved to primary-sources. Riding technique and traffic law only — carries no exam metadata, no question count and no passing score.

xx-msf-brc-handbook.title: MSF Basic RiderCourse Rider Handbook
xx-msf-brc-handbook.note: $3 purchase. Student handbook, not the instructor-only RiderCoach Guide. Cite only; not redistributable, no verbatim excerpts on-site.

xx-msf-brc-overview.title: MSF Basic RiderCourse Overview
xx-msf-brc-overview.note: Rider-facing description of the BRC — format, what's provided, that it ends in a knowledge test and skills evaluation. Does not state the question count.

xx-msf-brcu-faq.title: MSF Basic RiderCourse Curriculum FAQ
xx-msf-brcu-faq.note: MSF curriculum doc (v3.13.14), mirrored by the U.S. Navy. Only source for the 25-item knowledge test — no FLHSMV page or FAC rule states a count. States a 25-item test at each of Level I and Level II, so how many a rider sits depends on the delivery option a Sponsor runs; isExamSectioned is null-with-source for that reason. Dated 2014; cite for curriculum structure only.

xx-nhtsa-mns-2011.title: NHTSA Model National Standards for Entry-Level Rider Training
xx-nhtsa-mns-2011.note: Report HS 811 503, August 2011 — the federal standard a Texas entry-level curriculum must meet, and the document behind the MNS2011 courseType token. A competency framework listing what a rider must know and be able to do; it carries no knowledge-test specification at all, which is why TX's exam fields are null with a source rather than a number. Saved to primary-sources. Scoped xx- because any state regulating to this standard cites the same document.
